name: 8th Light
summary: At AI Engineer World's Fair 2025, Travis Frisinger examined why LLM output can appear intelligent without demonstrating understanding. His talk connected that argument to ChatGPT-assisted programming and creative multimodal experiments, proposing coherence as a framework for interpreting model behavior.

name: Aech AI
summary: At AI Engineer Summit 2025, Aech AI's Steven Moon described enterprise agents operating within existing organizational security boundaries. His talk outlines how private-cloud infrastructure, Microsoft 365, Azure, and Active Directory can support provisioning, monitoring, and auditing agents like employees.

name: Entry Point AI
summary: At AI Engineer Summit 2023, Entry Point AI’s Mark Hennings presented no-code fine-tuning for practical business tasks. His talk compared fine-tuning with prompt engineering through considerations including prompt length, performance, cost, training datasets, and collaboration.

name: EyeLevel.ai
summary: At AI Engineer World's Fair 2024, EyeLevel.ai's Benjamin Fletcher examined enterprise RAG failures caused by poor document ingestion, lost context, and irrelevant retrieval. His talk presented an alternative retrieval approach, illustrated through an Air France customer-support copilot.

name: Hey AI
summary: At AI Engineer World's Fair 2026, Veronica Hylak of Hey AI addressed how founders can make agentic-AI products understandable to customers. Her talk framed product storytelling around recognizable customer problems and specific workflow changes, with examples spanning security operations and AI-agent observability.

name: Isadora & Co | The Bloom House AI
Lindy
summary: At AI Engineer Summit 2023, Lindy’s Flo Crivello contrasted generative content tools with assistants that perform administrative work, including a meeting coordination demonstration. He argued that agentic AI could make business creation more accessible to individuals and small teams.

name: Method Financial
summary: At AI Engineer Summit 2025, Method Financial's Mustafa Ali joined OpenPipe's Kyle Corbitt to discuss scaling agents that process unstructured liability data. Their session describes an initial GPT-4 workflow whose production costs and prompt-engineering limitations prompted discussion of fine-tuned open-source models.

name: OpenClaw; TextCortex at the time of recording
Orbis Operations
summary: Luis Romero-Sevilla's appearance at AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 centers on Extended Cache Augmented Generation (ECAG) for rapidly changing, interconnected document collections. He presents parallel cached context buckets queried by a supervising model that synthesizes answers, contrasting the approach with vector-based RAG and GraphRAG.

name: Pfizer
summary: At AI Engineer Summit 2025, Pfizer’s Jonathan Lowe joined Neo4j’s Stephen Chin to discuss grounding enterprise generative AI with knowledge graphs and GraphRAG. The discussion connected life-sciences manufacturing and knowledge-transfer challenges with graph-based document chunking and contextual retrieval.

name: Pulley
summary: At AI Engineer World's Fair 2025, Charlie Guo described using Pulley sales-call transcripts to sharpen customer profiles and extract customer intelligence in two weeks. The analysis became a reusable internal tool with search, filters, and exports.

name: Synth
summary: At AI Engineer World's Fair 2025, Josh Purtell presented stateful environments for vertical agents working over long horizons. His talk describes how simplified representations of external systems such as Excel can preserve useful state, drawing on reinforcement-learning environments and agent benchmarks.

name: Witan Labs
summary: At AI Engineer Europe 2026, Nuno Campos presented Witan Labs' work on financial-spreadsheet agents, combining spreadsheet rendering, a high-fidelity C# engine, and a persistent Node.js REPL. The talk traces improvements through better search, formula tracing, systematic evaluation, and debugging.
